note: One-stop early voting opened 19 days before Election Day in both 2022 (Oct 20) and 2026 (Oct 15), so NCSBE's 'this time in 2022' comparison lines up by days-before. SB 747 (effective 2024) ended the 3-day post-election grace period for mail ballots (must arrive by Election Day) and added address-verification/ID steps for same-day registrants at one-stop sites; 2026 mail returns run below 2022 at every aligned point.

Same-day registration: NCSBE guidance gives same-day registrants whose verification card comes back undeliverable a chance to prove their address before final canvass (court-ordered change to SB 747's undeliverable-mail provision).

NCSBE counts only accepted ballots; Call the Map notes ballots awaiting cure/review are excluded. Latest tracker values (not official reports): Call the Map 1,101,318 through Oct 21; TPSI 1,101,321 as of Oct 22. The NCSBE 2026-10-22 report URL could not be fetched.

Calendar shift: 2026 early voting opened Tue Oct 13 (21 days before Election Day); 2022 opened Mon Oct 17 (22 days before). Same-day-of-voting and same-days-before alignments therefore differ by one day. SB 202 (2021) rules applied in both cycles, so it is not a 2022-vs-2026 difference for the early period.

Revisions: the 2022 first-day in-person count was 131,318 in the Oct 18, 2022 release but 134,962 when cited by the SoS in 2026 (a third value, 134,655, is attributed to UF's McDonald in a secondary source). Contemporaneous 2022 releases are lower than later-reconciled 2022 data; mixing them overstates 2026 growth slightly.

TexPolls matches by numbered day of early voting (day 1 with day 1); in 2022 and 2026 day 3 also falls 13 days before Election Day, so both alignments coincide. TexPolls notes Texas expanded required early-voting hours after 2022, so the comparison is not exact. Early voting ran Oct 19-30, 2026 (TX SoS).

Dallas County's state summary (267,593 in-person) differs from the county early-voter roster (198,398); TexPolls uses the roster. TPSI shows a higher Texas figure (2,270,617 as of Oct 22), from a later snapshot.

2026 includes statewide early in-person voting (sites open statewide Sat Oct 24 through Sun Nov 1; a few jurisdictions opened earlier - 96 early-site votes by Oct 20). 2022 had only absentee voting before Election Day, so the MI-SOS-returned series is kept to mail/absentee returns for both years. From Oct 24 on, 2026 totals should add early in-person votes.

Administrative change: in 2026 early voting is run by the Recorder's office (Justin Heap) and Election Day voting by the county Elections Department, under a power-sharing agreement reached this summer; in 2022 both early-ballot returns and tabulation releases came from the Elections Department. About 1.9 million early ballots were mailed on Oct 7, 2026; 1.9 million were mailed in 2022 (Oct 24, 2022 release). 3,126 ballots were mailed about a week early by vendor error.

SB 90 (2021) made standing vote-by-mail requests lapse after the 2022 general, so 2022 mail volume is not comparable with 2024/2026 (per Call the Map). Florida's in-person early voting is mandated Oct 24-31, 2026, with optional earlier county days.

Big source discrepancy: the official FL DOS PublicStats compiled 10/22/2026 08:05 (cumulative through prior day) shows Voted VBM 1,130,457 and Voted Early 552,198 (outstanding VBM 1,311,211). Trackers for Oct 22 show 1.86M-1.98M (TPSI 1,974,677: mail 1,211,084, in person 763,593). The gap is probably timing and county-level sourcing (an inference). The official 2022 archive is a single undated final snapshot (VBM 2,773,948; Early 2,285,465), so it cannot serve as a pace series.
Call the Map's CO counts are ballots returned to clerks before signature acceptance. All-mail state in both years.

TPSI 'pace' compares each state 'with its own 2022 count at the same number of days before Election Day' using 'each state's published 2022 and 2024 early vote checkpoints'. Call the Map mixes rules: same day of voting (IA, FL, MD, NC), same working day (ME), same days-before (NV, CO). Their pace percentages differ (e.g., NC +24% TPSI vs +38% Call the Map; WI +19% vs +6%).
